Package a kernel, initrd, firmware and authenticated command line for Raspberry
Pi.

## Inputs

| Name      | Kind      | Description                                                                                  |
| --------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `config`  | file      | Firmware config.txt selecting kernel8.img and initrd, including any board-specific settings. |
| `boot`    | directory | Raspberry Pi firmware tree containing start4.elf, fixup4.dat, DTBs, and overlays.            |
| `kernel`  | file      | ARM64 Linux kernel image.                                                                    |
| `initrd`  | file      | Initrd implementing the verified-root boot contract.                                         |
| `cmdline` | file      | Authenticated kernel command line.                                                           |

## Outputs

| Name   | Kind      | Description                          |
| ------ | --------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `tree` | directory | Contents of the signed boot ramdisk. |

## Execution

| Setting      | Value        |
| ------------ | ------------ |
| Environment  | Rugix Bakery |
| Source epoch | Consumed     |
| Output cache | Allowed      |

## Behavior

Prepare the contents of a signed Raspberry Pi 4/CM4 or Pi 5 boot image. The
`boot` input supplies `start4.elf`, `fixup4.dat`, device trees (`*.dtb`), and an
`overlays` directory. The rule copies these with the supplied kernel, initrd,
and authenticated command line.

The `config` input supplies the complete inner `config.txt`. It is copied
verbatim, so board settings and selected overlays remain under the caller's
control. Select `kernel8.img` and load `initrd`; those are the filenames used
for the kernel and initrd inputs. For example:

```ini title="config.txt"
[all]
arm_64bit=1
kernel=kernel8.img
initramfs initrd followkernel
dtoverlay=my-board
```

UART is enabled only when the supplied configuration requests it.

The exported `tree` is unsigned. Package it with `core/image-fat` and sign that
image with `core/sign-rpi`. Firmware trust provisioning remains separate.

## Example

For example, prepare a Pi boot tree:

```toml
uses = "core/prepare-rpi-boot"
inputs.boot = { path = "firmware" }
inputs.kernel = { path = "kernel" }
inputs.initrd = { path = "initrd" }
inputs.cmdline = { path = "cmdline" }
inputs.config = { path = "config.txt" }
```

Save the invocation as `build-rule.toml` and run
`./run-bakery bake rule build-rule.toml build/result`.
